title: ICJ orders provisional measures in South Africa v Israel genocide case
body:
On 26 January 2024, the International Court of Justice issued an order on provisional measures in the case brought by South Africa against Israel under the Genocide Convention. The court did not order a ceasefire, but said Israel must take all measures within its power to prevent acts covered by Article 2 of the Convention, ensure its troops do not commit such acts, prevent and punish incitement to genocide, allow more humanitarian aid into Gaza and preserve evidence.

Fifteen of the 17 judges backed all the measures. Julia Sebutinde of Uganda voted against all of them. Israeli judge Aharon Barak voted for two measures, saying he was convinced there was no plausibility of genocide. The court ordered Israel to report on its steps within one month. The ruling did not decide whether genocide had occurred, a question that may take years to resolve. The court's orders are legally binding but it has no direct mechanism of enforcement.

Al Jazeera reported that Israel's military action had killed more than 26,000 Palestinians since 7 October, without naming a separate source for the figure. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu criticised the ruling, saying Israel has an inherent right to defend itself and calling the attempt to deny that right blatant discrimination against the Jewish state. The hearings had been held on 11 and 12 January 2024.
